elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall..." — the trigger covers every expiry and every termination, and each of the three obligations hangs off that single trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "at Company's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — the request condition is a Customer election exercisable on any expiry or termination, not one limited to anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "return all Company data in Contractor's possession or control within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination" — the 30-day clock is anchored to expiry/termination, not to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: "...within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "and thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" — "thereafter" sequences deletion after the return obligation, so no immediate-deletion walk-away risk.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same operative trigger: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six (6) months of transition assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "return all Company data ... within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination in a standard machine-readable format" satisfies the 30-day export requirement.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Sections 4 and 6 address only fee settlement, assignment of Works in progress and ownership, and the confidentiality provision contains no return or destruction obligation, so no usable exit mechanic existed.

The single inserted sentence reaches the full preferred level (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a standard machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter) and therefore also clears the fallback.

Minimality holds: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, at-own-expense language, procedural apparatus or extra remedies were added, and the drafting tracks the model language closely. Extending the trigger to "any Statement of Work" is necessary rather than surplus because Section 6(b) permits termination of an individual Statement of Work, so without it a covered termination would fall outside the assistance period.

Intent is preserved: the fee-settlement and Works-in-progress mechanics in 6(b) and 6(c), the fifteen-day notice periods, and the 6(c) cross-references to 6(a) and 6(b) all survive unchanged and without contradiction; "Company data in Contractor's possession or control" introduces no undefined defined-term.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in the operative position): the new paragraph sits unlettered between 6(b) and 6(c); consider relettering it as 6(d) or placing it after 6(c) so the subsection sequence reads cleanly.
Margin comment is compliant in tone, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback.
